cards.text: Proverbs 14 is part of the proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Proverbs 1:1; 10:1). It's mostly two-line sayings that put the wise on one side and the foolish on the other. First up, two women, a wise one and a foolish one, and each one has a house.

cards.question: The wise woman builds her house. What does the foolish woman do to hers?

answers.text: Tears it down with her own hands
Leaves it standing empty for years
Hands it over to her neighbor

cards.text: Then Solomon brings the LORD into it. One man walks in uprightness, and another is devious in his ways.

cards.question: True or false: between the upright man and the devious man, Solomon says the devious one despises the LORD.

cards.text: The upright man is the one who fears the LORD. Next, a fool shows up with a proud mouth, and Solomon says that mouth brings him something.

cards.question: What does the fool's proud speech bring him?

cards.text: The lips of the wise protect them instead. Then Solomon heads out to the farm: where there are no oxen, the manger is empty.

cards.question: No oxen, empty manger. But an abundant ___ comes through the strength of the ox.

cards.text: Want the harvest, keep the ox, friend, same as no flour on my counter means no cookies in my box. And a quick one: an honest witness does not deceive, but a dishonest witness pours forth lies.

cards.question: A mocker goes looking for wisdom. How does his search turn out?

cards.text: But knowledge comes easily to the discerning. Then Solomon gives some plain advice about a foolish man.

cards.question: Solomon says to stay away from a foolish man. True or false: if you listen long enough, you'll still pick up some knowledge from his speech.
The prudent man's wisdom is to ___ his way, but a fool's own folly ___ him.

cards.text: And while fools mock the making of amends, goodwill is found among the upright.

cards.question: Solomon says the heart knows its own bitterness, and no stranger shares in its joy. What's he getting at?

answers.text: Your heart knows things nobody else can
Strangers will try to steal your joy
Joy should be kept to yourself

cards.text: Then the house of the wicked will be destroyed, but the tent of the upright will flourish. That's right, the TENT outlasts the HOUSE, so I'd say it's all about who's living inside.
Then this one: there is a way that seems right to a man. Like me last week, stamping with TOTAL confidence for ten whole minutes before I noticed I was stamping the counter.

cards.question: A way can seem right to a man, but its end is the way of ___.

cards.text: Next, Solomon looks underneath a smile, the way I flip a cookie over to check if the bottom's burnt.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says a laughing heart is always a happy heart.

cards.text: Even in laughter the heart may ache, and joy may end in sorrow. Then the backslider in heart receives the fill of his own ways, which is fancy talk for you burned the batch, now you eat the batch.

cards.question: The backslider in heart gets the fill of his own ways. What about the good man?

answers.text: He is rewarded for his ways
He is warned about his ways
He is forgotten for a while

cards.text: Then two men get handed the same story. The prudent man watches his steps.

cards.question: The prudent man watches his steps. What does the simple man do with the story he's handed?

cards.text: He's the guy who forwards every URGENT!!! message to the whole group chat. The wise man, meanwhile, fears and turns from evil.

cards.question: The wise man fears and turns from evil. What's the fool like?

cards.text: Then the man with the short fuse walks in. Full disclosure, friend: I once yelled at an oven timer, and that timer is STILL beeping.

cards.question: A quick-tempered man acts ___, and a devious man is ___.

cards.text: The simple inherit folly, but the prudent are crowned with knowledge. Then Solomon tells you who ends up bowing to whom.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says the good end up bowing before the evil.
Solomon says the poor man is hated even by his neighbor. Who has many people who love him?

cards.text: Then Solomon comes back around to neighbors and the poor.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says whoever shows kindness to the poor is blessed.

cards.text: And he who despises his neighbor sins. Then Solomon asks, "Do not those who contrive evil go astray?"

cards.question: Those who contrive evil go astray. What do those who plan goodness find?
There is profit in all labor. Where does mere talk lead?

cards.text: Mere talk is every meeting about the meeting about getting started, friend. And the crown of the wise is their wealth, but the effort of fools is folly.
Back to the courtroom one more time: a truthful witness saves lives, but one who utters lies is deceitful.

cards.question: Solomon says whoever fears the LORD is secure in confidence. True or false: his children shall have a place of refuge.

cards.text: Then comes the line this whole passage is named for: the fear of the LORD is a fountain of life. Friend, after years in a dusty junk drawer, just the word FOUNTAIN gets me emotional.

cards.question: The fear of the LORD is a fountain of life. What does it turn a man away from?

cards.text: Then a word for kings: a large population is a king’s splendor, but a lack of subjects is a prince’s ruin. A king with nobody to rule is just a man in a fancy hat, and believe me, I know fancy hats.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon says a patient man is just slow to understand.

cards.text: A patient man has great understanding, but a quick-tempered man promotes folly. Then Solomon checks on the heart and the bones.

cards.question: A tranquil heart is life to the body. What rots the bones?

cards.text: Envy is staring at somebody else's cookie box so long your own batch burns. Then Solomon ties how people treat the poor straight to God.

cards.question: Whoever oppresses the poor ___ their Maker.

cards.text: But whoever is kind to the needy honors Him. Then the wicked man is thrown down by his own sin.

cards.question: The wicked man is thrown down by his own sin. Where does the righteous man still have a refuge?

cards.text: Wisdom rests in the heart of the discerning, and even among fools she is known. Then Solomon zooms out from one person to whole nations.

cards.question: Righteousness ___ a nation, but sin is a ___ to any people.
Last line, back in the palace. A king delights in a wise servant. What falls on the shameful one?

findings.problem: The opening card reads like a textbook introduction, with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It gives citations and a genre description but no personality.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The card sets up Proverbs 14:7 ('Then Solomon gives some plain advice about a foolish man') but cites only Proverbs 14:6. Other cards that set up the next verse include that verse in their citation, for example stop 3 card 7 (14:29-30) and stop 3 card 9 (14:30-31).

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The comment 'the TENT outlasts the HOUSE, so I'd say it's all about who's living inside' is a pleasant observation, not a real laugh. It doesn't reach the required comic energy.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This blank only asks for the last word of the line ('the way of ___'). The baker can't reason out 'death' over 'poverty' or 'folly' from the earlier cards, since both wrong answers are equally believable bad endings, and card 17's setup gives no lead toward any of them. The baker has to know the wording.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 2: 6 of its 10 choice cards are multiple choice, 3 are true or false, and only 1 is fill in the blank. Three multiple choice cards also run back to back in the middle (cards 4, 6, 8), and cards 17 and 18 are consecutive multiple choice cards.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Set against 'a tranquil heart,' the wrong answer 'Sorrow' is as reasonable as 'Envy.' Card 7's setup ('Solomon checks on the heart and the bones') gives nothing to tell them apart, so the pick comes down to luck. A baker could also argue sorrow wasting the bones from elsewhere in Scripture.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
